en: to hold in one's arms; to embrace

examples.ko: 엄마가 우는 아이를 두 팔로 감싸안았어요.
examples.en: The mother held her crying child in both arms.

examples.ko: 그는 아픈 친구의 어깨를 감싸안고 위로했어요.
examples.en: He put his arm around his sick friend's shoulders and comforted him.

examples.ko: 추워서 무릎을 감싸안은 채 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: It was cold, so I sat hugging my knees.
It feels like the warm sunlight is embracing the village.

examples.ko: 실수한 후배를 감싸안아 주는 선배가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a senior who stands by a junior who made a mistake.

examples.ko: 서로의 다름을 감싸안을 수 있는 사회가 좋아요.
examples.en: I like a society that can embrace each other's differences.

explain: 그냥 '안다'보다 팔로 둘러 포근하게 안는 느낌이에요. 사람의 허물이나 다름을 너그럽게 받아들인다는 비유로도 써요. '감싸다'는 보호하거나 덮어 가린다는 쪽이라 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: I held the child tightly in my arms.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주다'를 붙여 상대를 위해 포근히 안는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 주다' means hugging someone warmly for their sake.

phrases.en: Mom is holding the baby in her arms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가슴 쪽으로 안는 모습을 말하는 비슷한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar expression for holding someone against the chest.

phrases.en: I warmly embraced my friend's pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 아픔이나 허물을 너그럽게 받아들인다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use meaning to generously accept someone's pain or faults.

explain_en: Compared with plain '안다', it feels like wrapping your arms around someone warmly. It is also used figuratively for generously accepting someone's faults or differences. '감싸다' leans toward protecting or covering something, so it is a little different.

examples.en: The child seems sleepy and keeps blinking.

examples.ko: 소가 큰 눈을 끔벅거리며 서 있어요.
examples.en: The cow stands there slowly blinking its big eyes.
The sunlight was dazzling, so I kept blinking.

examples.ko: 눈을 끔벅거리는 걸 보니 졸린가 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you blinking, you must be sleepy.
Grandfather just kept blinking without saying a word.
I was blinking sleepily and ended up falling asleep.

explain: '깜박이다'보다 느릿하고 둔하게 눈을 감았다 떠요. 졸리거나 멍할 때, 소처럼 눈이 큰 동물에게 잘 어울려요. '끔벅대다'도 같은 느낌으로 써요.

phrases.en: The cat blinks its sleepy eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끔벅거리다'와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the same meaning as '끔벅거리다'.

phrases.example: 그는 아무 말도 못 하고 눈만 끔벅거렸어요.
phrases.en: He couldn't say anything and just blinked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당황하거나 멍해서 말없이 눈만 깜박일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is flustered or dazed and only blinks silently.

phrases.en: The cow looks at me, blinking slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈을 끔벅이면서 다른 행동을 할 때 연결해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect slow blinking with another action.

explain_en: It means opening and closing the eyes, but feels slower and duller than '깜박이다'. It suits moments of sleepiness or daze, and animals with big eyes. '끔벅대다' is a similar word.

en: to sway; to flutter; to wave

examples.en: The laundry hung on the roof flutters in the wind.
His hair fluttered every time he ran.
I took photos in a flowing skirt.
The big shirt flaps around, so it's a bit uncomfortable.
The Korean flag is waving in front of the school.

examples.ko: 너풀거릴 정도로 큰 옷은 사지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't buy clothes so big that they flap around.

explain: 천이나 머리카락처럼 얇고 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 흔들릴 때 써요. 헐렁한 옷이 몸 주위에서 흔들리는 모습에도 잘 어울려요. '너울거리다'는 더 느리고 크게 물결치는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The baggy pants flap in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 지금 보이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing what you see right now.

phrases.en: I ran wearing a fluttering skirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸며서 가볍게 흔들리는 옷이나 천을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to describe light clothes or cloth that flutters.

phrases.en: The flag fluttered all day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 지나간 장면을 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form for a scene that has already passed.

explain_en: It is used when something thin and light, like cloth or hair, keeps moving in the wind. It also fits loose clothes flapping around the body. '너울거리다' feels slower and more wavelike.

t90.ax: I took photos in a flowing skirt.

examples.en: The players struggled hard to the end but sadly lost.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 가족을 위해 열심히 분투해요.
examples.en: He struggles hard for his family.

examples.ko: 작은 가게를 지키려고 분투하는 사장님이 계세요.
examples.en: There is an owner who is fighting hard to keep a small shop.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 우승을 위해 분투하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is striving hard to win the championship.
The story of struggling in a hard environment is moving.
Don't struggle alone; ask for help.

explain: 어려운 조건에서 힘을 다해 애쓰는 모습에 써요. 결과보다 노력하는 과정을 인정하는 느낌이라 스포츠 중계나 기사에 자주 나와요. '고군분투하다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: That person struggled hard all alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분투하다'에 '혼자 힘들게'라는 느낌이 더해진 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a sense of struggling hard alone.

phrases.en: The players who tried hard until the end are cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분투하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, everyday word for making an effort.

phrases.en: After a long struggle, I succeeded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 노력을 지나 결과가 나왔을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a result comes after hard effort.

explain_en: Use it for putting in all your strength under hard conditions. It recognizes the effort more than the result, so it often appears in sports commentary and articles. People also say '고군분투하다'.

t90.ax: He struggles hard for his family.

examples.en: The kids were playing with fire and almost started a big blaze.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 불장난하다 혼난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I got scolded for playing with fire.

examples.ko: 건조한 날에는 산 근처에서 불장난하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: On dry days, you must not play with fire near the mountains.

examples.ko: 동생이 라이터로 불장난하는 걸 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled to see my younger sibling playing with a lighter.

examples.ko: 그런 위험한 일은 불장난하듯 가볍게 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat a dangerous thing like that as lightly as a game with fire.
If you treat romance like a game with fire, both people get hurt.

explain: 말 그대로 불을 가지고 노는 것인데, 비유로 가벼운 마음으로 위험한 일이나 연애를 하는 것에도 써요. 어른이 아이를 혼낼 때 '불장난하면 안 돼'라고 많이 말해요. 비유로 쓸 때는 책임지지 않는 가벼운 태도를 비판하는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: That wasn't love, it was just a fling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 마음 없이 가볍게 시작한 위험한 관계나 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A risky relationship or act begun casually, without real commitment.

explain_en: It literally means playing with fire, and figuratively it covers doing something risky or having a romance with a careless attitude. Adults often scold children with '불장난하면 안 돼'. Used figuratively, it criticizes an irresponsible, casual attitude.

examples.en: The door creaks in the wind.
The old chair creaked every time I sat down.
The floor creaked, so I walked carefully.
The sound of the bed creaking woke me up.
The stairs creak, so please come down slowly.
The old bicycle creaked as it went up the hill.

explain: 문이나 마루, 의자 같은 것이 소리를 반복해서 내는 모습이에요. 소리가 한 번 날 때는 '삐거덕 소리가 나다'라고 해요. 같은 뜻으로 '삐걱거리다'도 써요.

phrases.en: The old bed creaks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and more common in daily use.

phrases.en: I heard a creaking sound at night and was scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삐거덕거리다'의 활용형으로, 소리를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing the sound.

phrases.en: The stairs creak, so I go up carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말하는 '-아서/어서' 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-aseo/eoseo' connecting form that gives a reason.

explain_en: It describes things like doors, floors and chairs making that creaking sound repeatedly. For a single creak you say '삐거덕 소리가 나다'. '삐걱거리다' is also used with the same meaning.

t90.ax: The door creaks in the wind.

en: desperate struggle; life-or-death struggle; battle for survival

examples.ko: 구조대는 밤새 폭우 속에서 사투를 벌였어요.
examples.en: The rescue team fought a desperate struggle in the heavy rain all night.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 끝없는 사투 끝에 결국 우승했어요.
examples.en: After an endless struggle, that player finally won the championship.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나는 건 저에게 매일이 사투였어요.
examples.en: For me, getting up in the morning was a battle every day.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 생존을 건 사투가 이어졌어요.
examples.en: A fight for survival went on at the top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 그는 병과의 사투에서 끝내 이겨 냈어요.
examples.en: He finally won his fight against the illness.

examples.ko: 오랜 사투로 얻은 합격이라 더 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm even happier because I earned this pass through a long struggle.

explain: 주로 '사투를 벌이다' 꼴로 쓰고, 목숨을 걸 만큼 필사적인 싸움이에요. 일상에서는 '졸음과의 사투'처럼 조금 과장해서 말하기도 해요. 방언을 뜻하는 '사투리'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.example: 긴 사투 끝에 구조대가 아이를 구했어요.
phrases.en: After a long life-or-death struggle, the rescue team saved the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 싸움이 끝난 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the outcome after a hard fight.

phrases.en: I fought a desperate battle against sleepiness while driving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 조금 과장해서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly exaggerated everyday expression.

phrases.example: 의사들이 환자를 살리려고 사투를 벌이는 중이에요.
phrases.en: The doctors are fighting desperately to save the patient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 필사적으로 싸우고 있다는 진행형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Progressive form: fighting desperately right now.
phrases.en_equiv: in the middle of a desperate fight

explain_en: It is mostly used as '사투를 벌이다', a fight so desperate it is as if life were at stake. In daily talk people exaggerate a bit, as in '졸음과의 사투' (a battle against sleepiness). It is a different word from '사투리' (dialect), so don't mix them up.

examples.en: He left without saying a single word.
Let alone an apology, there wasn't even a word of explanation.
Couldn't you have at least said a word beforehand?

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 일언반구조차 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't say so much as a word about that matter.
My friend didn't answer with even a word, so I felt hurt.

examples.ko: 회사에서 일언반구 통보도 없이 계약을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The company ended the contract without any notice at all.

explain: 거의 항상 '없다, 않다' 같은 부정의 말과 함께 써서 '한마디도 없이'라는 섭섭함이나 불만을 나타내요. '일언반구도 없이', '일언반구 말이 없다'처럼 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '한마디도'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 그 일에 대해 일언반구도 하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He didn't say a single word about that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝까지 말을 하지 않았다는 섭섭함이나 불만을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses disappointment that nothing was said at all.

phrases.example: 몇 번을 물어봐도 일언반구 대답이 없어요.
phrases.en: No matter how many times I ask, there is no answer at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문에 아무 반응이 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is no response at all to a question.

phrases.en: My friend left without saying a word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '일언반구도 없이' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday alternative to 일언반구도 없이.

explain_en: It almost always goes with a negative such as '없다' or '않다', expressing disappointment or complaint that there was not even one word. It appears as '일언반구도 없이' or '일언반구 말이 없다'. In everyday talk people say '한마디도'.

examples.en: The skin of the apple got scratched.
Don't judge people just by their outside.

examples.ko: 이 책은 거죽이 낡았지만 내용은 좋아요.
examples.en: This book's cover is worn, but the content is good.

examples.ko: 수박 거죽을 두드려 보면 익었는지 알아요.
examples.en: If you knock on the surface of a watermelon, you can tell if it's ripe.
The sofa covering tore, so I put on a new one.
The outside is fine, but the inside is all rotten.

explain: '겉'과 비슷하지만 속과 대비해서 겉모습이나 겉껍질을 말할 때 자주 써요. 반의어는 '속'이에요. '겉'보다 말투가 조금 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 과일은 겉이 깨끗해도 속이 상할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Fruit can be spoiled inside even if the outside looks clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거죽'보다 말투가 부드럽고 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer in tone than 거죽 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: The surface of the wall peeled off, so we repainted it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉껍질이나 겉면이 떨어질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for an outer layer or surface coming off.

phrases.example: 거죽과 속이 다른 사람은 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: It's hard to trust people whose outside and inside are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반의어 '속'과 함께 써서 겉모습과 실제를 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with its opposite 속 to contrast appearance and reality.

explain_en: It is close to '겉' but is often used when contrasting the outside with the inside. Its opposite is '속'. It can sound a little rougher than '겉'.

t90.ax: The skin of the apple got scratched.

examples.en: The security guard has a baton on his belt.
The rhythmic gymnast threw the clubs and caught them.
The club routine looks really difficult.
This club is made of plastic, so it is very light.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 곤봉으로 하는 체조를 배웠어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I learned gymnastics with clubs.

examples.ko: 경찰이 곤봉을 들고 입구 앞에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A police officer was standing at the entrance holding a baton.

explain: 경비원이나 경찰이 쓰는 짧은 막대, 그리고 리듬체조 도구를 모두 곤봉이라고 해요. 일반적인 막대기는 '몽둥이'나 '방망이'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 곤봉을 휘두르는 장면이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: A scene of police swinging batons was on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤봉을 크게 흔들 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for swinging a club widely.

phrases.example: 경찰 곤봉은 보통 허리에 차고 있어요.
phrases.en: Police batons are usually worn at the waist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이나 경비원이 쓰는 막대를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the stick used by police or guards.

phrases.example: 리듬체조 곤봉은 두 개를 같이 써요.
phrases.en: In rhythmic gymnastics, two clubs are used together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체조 도구를 말할 때 앞에 '리듬체조'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '리듬체조' in front when talking about the gymnastics equipment.

explain_en: '곤봉' covers both the short stick used by guards and police and the clubs used in rhythmic gymnastics. A plain stick is more often called '몽둥이' or '방망이'.

t90.ax: The club routine looks really difficult.

en: to be sick all the time

examples.en: My grandmother has been unwell all the time lately.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 골골해서 학교를 자주 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I was sickly as a child, so I often missed school.

examples.ko: 골골한 사람이 오래 산다는 말도 있어요.
examples.en: There is a saying that sickly people live long.
My body is weak, so I feel ill every time the seasons change.

examples.ko: 골골해 보이지만 사실은 건강 검진 결과가 좋아요.
examples.en: He looks frail, but actually his health checkup results are good.

examples.ko: 일이 많은 달에는 늘 골골하게 지내요.
examples.en: In busy months I always go around feeling under the weather.

explain: '아프다'와 달리 크게 아픈 건 아니지만 늘 기운이 없고 자주 앓는 상태에 써요. 반대말은 '튼튼하다'예요. 말투가 가벼워서 '골골거리다'와 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling has been feeling sickly for several days because of a cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골골하다'와 뜻이 같지만 말투가 더 가벼워서 편한 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 골골하다 but sounds lighter, so it suits casual conversation.

phrases.example: 저는 몸이 약해서 늘 골골한 편이에요.
phrases.en: I'm physically weak, so I tend to be sickly all the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편이다'를 붙이면 자주 아픈 편이라고 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '편이다' softly says that you tend to be sickly.

phrases.en: These days I exercise, so I'm not sickly anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 쓰면 예전과 달리 자주 아프지 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says you no longer get sick often.

explain_en: Unlike '아프다', it means not seriously ill but constantly low on energy and often unwell. Its opposite is '튼튼하다'. The tone is light, and it is used much like '골골거리다'.

t90.ax: There is a saying that sickly people live long.

en: to be rather bent; to be rather arched

examples.en: My grandfather's back is a little bent, but he walks fast.
After sitting for a long time, my shoulders got hunched.
If you study with a hunched posture, your neck hurts.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 키가 큰데 늘 구부정하게 서 있어요.
examples.en: He is tall, but he always stands with a stoop.

examples.ko: 친구가 내 등이 구부정하다고 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend told me my back is a bit hunched.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 몸이 구부정해지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think the body gets more bent as people age.

explain: 허리나 등처럼 사람 몸이 조금 굽은 모습에 주로 써요. 반대는 '꼿꼿하다'예요. 물건이 휜 모양은 보통 '구부러지다', '휘다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: A slouched posture is bad for your health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허리나 등이 조금 굽은 자세를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a posture with a slightly bent back.

phrases.en: Don't sit hunched; straighten your back.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구부정하게'는 동사 앞에 쓰는 부사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, used before a verb.

phrases.en: That person's shoulders look a bit hunched.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it looks that way from the outside.

explain_en: It is mostly used for a person's body, such as a back or waist that is slightly bent. The opposite is '꼿꼿하다' (upright). For bent objects, people usually say '구부러지다' or '휘다'.

examples.ko: 편지를 읽던 할머니가 눈시울을 붉히며 흐느끼셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma, reading the letter, sobbed with reddened eyes.
Listening to the song, my eyes grew warm with tears.
My friends' eyes got moist at the graduation.
My father's eyes turned slightly red.
My eyes sting with emotion at the touching story.

examples.ko: 눈시울이 젖은 채로 그는 웃어 보였어요.
examples.en: He smiled with his eyes still moist.

explain: 눈 가장자리를 뜻하지만, 거의 감동하거나 슬플 때 눈물이 날 것 같은 모습에만 써요. '눈시울이 붉어지다/뜨거워지다/젖다'가 자주 붙는 말이에요. 단순히 눈 모양을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그는 옛 친구를 만나고 눈시울을 붉혔어요.
phrases.en: He teared up when he met his old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물이 날 만큼 감동하거나 슬퍼한다는 뜻이고, 눈물이 흐르기 전의 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means being moved or sad enough to get teary, typically before tears actually fall.

explain_en: It means the rim of the eye, but it is used almost only for moments of being moved or sad when tears are about to come. It commonly pairs with '붉어지다/뜨거워지다/젖다'. You don't use it to describe eye shape.

examples.en: I got hit in the stomach and the pit of my stomach really hurts.
I ate too fast, and the area around my solar plexus feels stuffy.
Please don't press hard on the pit of my stomach.
When I'm nervous, the bottom of my breastbone throbs and stings.

examples.ko: 의사가 명치 부분을 살짝 눌러 봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor gently pressed on the area of my solar plexus.
Maybe it's indigestion; it feels like something is stuck in the pit of my stomach.

explain: 가슴뼈 아래, 배 윗부분 가운데를 가리켜요. 체했을 때나 맞았을 때 '배'라고 하기보다 '명치가 아프다'고 정확히 말해요. '명치끝'이라고도 하고, 병원에서도 이 위치를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: My upper stomach hurts; maybe I have indigestion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸이 아픈 위치를 정확히 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to name the exact spot that hurts.
phrases.en_equiv: to have pain in the pit of the stomach

phrases.en: I got hit in the solar plexus by the ball and couldn't breathe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동이나 싸움에서 그 부위를 세게 맞았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when that spot is hit hard in sports or a fight.
phrases.en_equiv: to be hit in the solar plexus

phrases.en: The tip of my solar plexus feels tight and sore.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명치'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만 가슴뼈 아래 끝부분을 조금 더 정확히 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, but points a bit more precisely to the lower tip of the breastbone.
phrases.en_equiv: the very pit of the stomach

explain_en: It points to the middle of the upper abdomen, just below the breastbone. When you have indigestion or got hit, people say '명치가 아프다' to be precise instead of just '배'. It is also said as '명치끝', and used at hospitals to describe this spot.

examples.en: The baby squirms in the bed, refusing to sleep.
He struggled with all his might to escape poverty.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘 때 몸부림치는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of thrashing around when I sleep.
No matter how much I struggled, the situation didn't improve.
After struggling desperately to survive, he finally succeeded.

examples.ko: 몸부림치며 울던 아이를 엄마가 안아 줬어요.
examples.en: The mother hugged the child who had been crying and thrashing.

explain: 아파서 또는 화가 나서 몸을 마구 비틀 때 쓰고, 힘든 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습에 비유로도 많이 써요. 명사 '몸부림'을 써서 '몸부림을 치다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The baby thrashes around while sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸부림치다'를 '몸부림을 치다'로 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A split form of 몸부림치다.

phrases.en: I flailed in the water to survive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손발을 마구 움직이며 애쓰는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes frantically moving limbs while struggling.

phrases.example: 아이는 장난감을 사 달라고 몸부림치며 울었어요.
phrases.en: The child cried and writhed, asking for a toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 다른 행동과 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -며, it links to another action.

explain_en: It can mean twisting your body wildly from pain or anger, and it is often used figuratively for struggling hard to escape a difficult situation. You can also use the noun and say '몸부림을 치다'.
